title: Foxrun Diagnostics integration scratchnotes
content:
Context: quick working capture after 2025-10-16 intro call with Foxrun Diagnostics (clinical device manufacturer). They want a private deployment inside AWS account with strict PHI handling, bursty inference for triage assistant, and 99.9% uptime SLA for daytime hours. Notes are messy — cleaning into a proper SOW next week.

Attendees:
- Foxrun: Mira Sato (CTO), Daniel Ortiz (Platform lead), Lina Chen (Security/compliance)
- Redwood: Nate Cheng (SE, lead), Priya Menon (solutions arch), Jonas Keller (deploy eng)

High level ask (verbatim from Mira):
- "We need a private inference endpoint that never touches our customer data outside our VPC. Latency under 300ms p95 for triage queries, ~50 RPS sustained during working hours, with daily burst allowances up to 200 RPS for 2–5 minute windows."

Immediate red flags / gotchas raised on call:
1) Data residency + PHI: Foxrun requires all logs and telemetry to be routed to their internal SIEM; no PII/PHI can be mirrored to Redwood hosted control plane. Need KMS/HSM integration for model keys and ability to disable diagnostic telemetry.
2) NAT/bandwidth: Their infra team uses a central NAT + proxy which previously throttled long-lived streaming connections. Streaming/long-poll fallback needs verification (we may need to recommend private ALB with TLS termination in customer's account).
3) Model choice constraints: They want medical-grade LLM (clinical SOP style answers). They asked if we can use a quantized open model (7B q4) to hit latency targets. Concern: hallucination risk and auditability of token traces.
4) Cold-start concerns for dedicated pools: warmup scripts/training prompts to preload KV caches necessary to hit p95 SLA for first requests after deploy.
5) Deployment window: Foxrun prefers maintenance windows 0100–0400 PT; rollout plan must respect that.

Technical metrics / rough numbers they shared:
- Typical prompt length: 150–400 tokens; average response 60–120 tokens
- Peak seq len observed: 1024 tokens for occasional long-case summaries
- Target latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms (end-to-end, application-to-response)
- Desired throughput: 50 RPS steady, bursts to 200 RPS for up to 5 minutes, approx. 30k tokens/minute average during bursts
- Retention: audit logs for 7 years (legal).

Preliminary feasibility notes (internal):
- Model sizing: likely need mix of capacities — a quantized 13B (q4) may be safer for quality but might not hit p95 at 50 RPS on a single GPU; prefer scaled Dedicated pool (2–4 x A100-class or H100 depending on customer hw preference). Provide model variant routing: high-cost high-quality (13B fp16 or 13B q4/8) + cheap fallback (7B q4) for non-critical path.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated triage prompts will cut costs; need to instrument hit-rate early. Warmup should include typical case templates (we should ask for 10 canonical prompts).
- Networking: Must run Control Plane in private mode — propose Private deployment (customer-managed control plane in their VPC) with minimal telemetry forwarded out. Confirm if we can support control-plane-to-redwood for billing only (tokenized metadata) or whether they want zero egress.
- Keys: KMS integration mandatory. Confirm HSM requirement (Lina flagged HSM for key custody).

Open questions for Foxrun (action: Priya to send list by 2026-03-10):
- Confirm explicit egress policy: can any non-essential telemetry be sent to Redwood for support? If yes, which fields? (we should send a proposed telemetry strip template)
- Provide 10 canonical prompts + expected ideal answer length for warmup cache and regression tests.
- Exact SLA window: is 99.9% targeted across 24h or only 0900–1900 PT? Need clarity for pricing.
- Consent/legal: sample BAA/DPAs required? Provide legal contact.

Short-term next steps (owner / due):
- Priya: draft an architecture diagram for Private deployment in customer account with note on ALB/TLS termination, KMS flow, and telemetry opt-out. Due 2026-03-12. (P0)
- Nate: prototype warmup script + sample benchmark using 13B-quant model in our staging (simulate 50 RPS + 200 RPS bursts) and capture p95 numbers. Due 2026-03-19. (P0)
- Jonas: check if Private control plane can be configured to forward only billing metrics (no payload or token traces). Confirm HSM connectors we support. Due 2026-03-15. (P1)
- Foxrun action: send canonical prompts and sample PHI redaction rules (Mira/Daniel). Requested by 2026-03-11.

Longer-term items / pricing considerations:
- Dedicated reserved capacity estimate: ballpark monthly commit for 2xA100-equivalent to meet 50 RPS p95 — draft quote once we have target model (estimate: $XXk/month — placeholder). Need input from sales for exact T-shirt pricing.
- Observability: they want logs to their SIEM. We'll propose a shipper that runs in-customer-account and forwards only selected fields (no content) to their SIEM.
- Eval + safety: propose a small eval contract (30 days) to measure hallucination/regression rates against a shared test-set. Tie regression thresholds to rollback policies (Redwood rollouts).

Notes for later write-up (SOW / security appendix):
- Include explicit list of data flows and which fields are sanitized.
- Include SLA definitions (what counts as outage, warmup window behavior, scheduled maintenance exclusions).
- Include disaster recovery: cross-AZ deployment, optional cross-region failover (but note that cross-region may violate residency).

Random observations / scribbles from the Q&A:
- Daniel asked about token-level cost attribution by route; good sales hook — emphasize route-level billing in the quote.
- Lina asked if we can support a policy to never store conversation content in any persistent logs; we can if customer deploys private control plane and we run the shipper in their account.
- Mira: interested in on-prem option later (air-gapped). Flag for product: document on-prem packaging differences for build of HSM + network isolation.

Risks to track:
- If they enforce strict zero-egress, Redwood support will be limited; expect longer onboarding and higher support runbook cost.
- Model quality vs latency tradeoff: if they insist on medically precise answers, we may need larger model footprint and higher cost — must make this explicit in proposal.

Quick checklist before next call:
[ ] Send architecture diagram (Priya)
[ ] Baseline perf numbers (Nate)
[ ] Confirm control plane telemetry options (Jonas)
[ ] Get canonical prompts + PHI policy from Foxrun

Next sync: schedule 30–45m enterprise technical call w/ Foxrun infra + legal + Redwood eng. Target calendar week starting 2026-03-22 (TBD).

Scratch closing note: keep this doc ephemeral — once SOW & solution deck drafted, move notes to confluence page CONFLUENCE-FTX-8421 and attach prompt corpus.

End of notes.
